questions.q: Identify the protagonist's full name and profession as explicitly stated in the opening paragraphs of "उद्देश का नक्षत्र".
questions.a: The protagonist is आयुर्विज्ञान, an Ayurvedic physician (वैद्य) running a government dispensary (उद्देश का नक्षत्र). A wrong answer like "ओंकारनाथ" or "डॉक्टर" reveals confusion between the two male leads or failure to distinguish Ayurvedic from allopathic practice - a critical distinction for the story's central conflict.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why आयुर्विज्ञान refuses the inspector's order to use the new allopathic medicines, connecting his refusal to his professional identity.
questions.a: आयुर्विज्ञान refuses because his professional identity as a वैद्य is inseparable from his ethical commitment to his patients' trust and his ancestral knowledge system; compliance would violate both his conscience and the therapeutic relationship he has built. A wrong answer focusing only on "stubbornness" or "pride" misses the philosophical depth - this isn't ego but epistemological resistance to colonial medical hegemony.

questions.q: Apply the "action-revelation" method: Select ONE specific action by आयुर्विज्ञान in the clinic confrontation scene and analyze what it reveals about his character that his words alone don't show.
questions.a: When आयुर्विज्ञान "अपनी कुर्सी पर बैठा रहा" (remained seated in his chair) while the inspector shouted, this physical stillness reveals deeper resolve than his verbal arguments - it shows embodied resistance, professional dignity, and refusal to be intimidated by colonial authority. A wrong answer quoting only his dialogue misses how Premchand uses body language to characterize quiet strength versus performative outrage.

questions.q: Compare आयुर्विज्ञान's relationship with his father (फिरकथ) versus his relationship with ओंकारनाथ. What does this contrast reveal about his core values?
questions.a: With his father, आयुर्विज्ञान shows reverent obedience and emotional vulnerability ("पिता के चरणों में गिर पड़ा"); with ओंकारनाथ, he shows intellectual equality and moral firmness ("तुम्हारी नौकरी तुम्हारी जान से प्यारी है"). This contrast reveals he values tradition and filial duty emotionally, but professional integrity and intellectual honesty rationally - he negotiates with authority figures differently based on the nature of their claim on him.

questions.q: Evaluate whether आयुर्विज्ञान's resignation is a "victory" or "defeat" within the story's moral framework. Defend your judgment using textual evidence.
questions.a: It is a moral victory but material defeat - he loses livelihood (defeat) but retains self-respect and exposes colonial injustice (victory). The text frames it as victory: "उसने अपनी आत्मा बेचने से इनकार कर दिया" and his father's final blessing "तूने कुल का नाम रखा". A wrong answer calling it pure tragedy misses Premchand's Gandhian ethos where spiritual integrity transcends material loss.

questions.q: Create a 50-word diary entry from आयुर्विज्ञान's perspective on the night before his resignation, capturing his internal conflict using his characteristic vocabulary (Sanskritized Hindi for professional thoughts, colloquial for emotional ones).
questions.a: A strong entry mixes registers: "कल निरीक्षक ने अंग्रेजी दवाओं का आदेश दिया। वैद्यकर्म मेरा धर्म है, नौकरी नहीं। पिता को क्या कहूं? माँ की चिंता... पर आत्मा तो अपनी है। कल त्यागपत्र दूंगा।" Weak entries use uniform language, missing how his code-switching reveals his fractured identity under colonialism.
